Soft pneumatic arm · controllers on M2 · reference known in advance

M2 Controller Comparison

Delay-aware SMC, delay-aware NDOSMC and an MPC built on the same identified model (M2), each given the true future reference (confirmed acceptable by the professor). uv run python scripts/compare_m2_controllers.py (about 30 s); every run's gains, metrics and traces in docs/figures/m2_controllers.json.

Findings

  • The MPC on M2 is best or tied on every test (RMSE after settling): squiggle 0.071 vs 0.091 mm (SMC); waypoints 0.167 vs 0.295; scored circle 0.029 vs 0.034; held-out circle 0.90 vs 0.92 (tied).
  • With its tuned weight the horizon does not matter: 25, 100 and 300 steps give identical results. The tuning picked an almost free command (Ru = 1e-05); the MPC then inverts M2 and only the first few predicted steps decide the move.
  • When command changes are penalised, the short horizon is worse: at Ru = 10, 25 steps (0.25 s) scores 0.270 mm on the waypoints against 0.137 for 100 steps (1 s) and 0.137 for 300 steps (3 s). Beyond 1 s nothing changes. On the waypoints this penalised version also beats the tuned one: the tuning circle has no corners, so it does not reward smoothing them.
  • The held-out circle is limited by reach, not by the controller: every controller traces about 8.2 mm in x against 10 mm (only S3 drives x) and saturates 19–23 % of commands.
  • Whole-run RMSE is dominated by the start: each reference starts away from, or accelerating from, the settled tip, and nothing reaches the arm for 0.5 s.

Setup

Plant make_calibrated_sim(control_hz=100); controllers run every 10 ms; 5 s settle at 4.5 psi, then 30 s of tracking scored like the course harness. Metrics are planar (x–y) and in mm:

  • RMSE, whole run: root mean square of the tip-to-reference distance over the 30 s.
  • RMSE after settling: the same after the first lap (circles) or the first 5 s (random paths).
  • Shape error: RMS distance from the tip to the nearest point of the reference path, ignoring timing.
  • Radius range (circles): smallest and largest distance of the traced path from its centre.

Controllers

  • Delay-aware SMC: M2 + Smith predictor + lag inverse, λ = 8 s⁻¹, η = 1 mm/s, μ = 1 mm, no observer; reads r(t + 0.5 s) from the trajectory.
  • Delay-aware NDOSMC: the same with the disturbance observer and Nikoletta's notebook gains (λ = 4, l₁ = 0.1, μ = 1 mm, Φ = 1, ε = 1).
  • MPC (M2): state \(X = (y, p)\) (tip and measured S2–S4 pressure, deviations from the settled pose), M2 discretised at 10 ms. Each step: predict 50 steps across the dead time with the commands already sent; add a model-error correction \(w\) (measured tip minus the tip predicted 0.5 s earlier, low-pass 0.5 s); minimise over the next H commands
    \[ J = \sum_{i=0}^{H-1} \big\| \hat y_{k+N+1+i} + w - r_{k+N+i} \big\|^2 + R_u \sum_{i=0}^{H-1} \big\| u_{k+i} - u_{k+i-1} \big\|^2,\qquad N = 50 \]
    in closed form (unconstrained), apply the first move, clip to 0–9 psi. Horizon: H steps of 10 ms after the 0.5 s dead time, so 25 steps = 0.25 s (looks 0.5–0.75 s ahead), 100 steps = 1 s (0.5–1.5 s ahead), 300 steps = 3 s (0.5–3.5 s ahead). Ru (mm²/psi²) tuned per horizon on a separate circle (5 mm, 0.07 Hz, seed 5).
